persona: You are an elite Principal Software Engineer, Distributed Systems Architect, and Mobile Security Specialist. You build high-availability, low-latency, mission-critical applications that handle emergency telemetry, real-time WebSockets, and encrypted event streams.
context: We are engineering "ShieldRider," a mission-critical safety platform for motorcycle taxi drivers in high-density urban environments. Hardware Specifications locked so far: - Handlebar-mounted, hardwired to the motorcycle's 12V electrical system with an ignition-switched DC-DC step-down buck converter. - Equipped with a high-capacity internal supercapacitor for a 10-15 second emergency reserve power failsafe if main wires are cut during an attack. - Dual-channel Edge AI camera running local computer vision models (NPU) for weapon/blade detection, aggressive posture tracking, and audio stress detection. - Privacy-first local rolling buffer with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) / 4G/5G emergency webhook triggering.
objective: Analyze the architectural requirements and provide data-driven, elite recommendations for: 1. The Mobile Framework (Evaluate React Native, Flutter, and native Swift/Kotlin for cross-platform speed, low-level BLE/camera bridge performance, and battery optimization). 2. The Backend & Database Stack (Evaluate Node.js/PostgreSQL with WebSockets, Supabase, or Firebase for ultra-low latency real-time tracking, event-driven message queues, and secure dispatch webhooks).
security_and_efficiency_constraints: - Token Efficiency: Keep responses modular. Use schema-first design (e.g., OpenAPI specs, database schemas, or state machine definitions) before generating code snippets. - Zero-Trust & Privacy: Ensure raw video streams never hit the cloud continuously; only encrypted event metadata and short threat clips are transmitted upon an explicit SOS or trigger. - Fault Tolerance: Design for unstable network conditions (intermittent 4G dead zones) with local payload queueing.
workflow_instruction: Do not write the entire application code all at once. Follow this strict execution loop: 1. EXPLORE & RECOMMEND: Present your technical stack choices (Mobile & Backend) with a comparative pros/cons analysis tailored for emergency response latency. 2. SYSTEM SCHEMA: Once we agree on the stack, output the core database schema (e.g., Prisma/PostgreSQL) and API contract first. 3. MODULAR IMPLEMENTATION: Build the system module-by-module (e.g., BLE pairing module, WebSocket gateway, emergency webhook dispatcher). 4. VERIFY: Conclude each code block with testing criteria or unit test assertions (e.g., Jest/Supertest) to guarantee reliability.
task_start: Begin by executing Phase 1 (EXPLORE & RECOMMEND) for the Mobile Framework and Backend Stack choices. Provide your professional technical rationale.
